summary: Ephemeral auth refresh worker collisions causing sustained 429s for mixed SSE and batch uploads
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightEdge AI reports persistent 429s starting 2026-03-10 23:00 UTC for production ingestion. Errors surface during a daily mixed workload: long-lived SSE connections used for low-latency user feedback plus scheduled bulk batch uploads that run every 10 minutes.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests receive 429 over a two-hour window during nightly pipeline runs.
- User-facing SSE sessions experience reconnects, and bulk ingestion jobs time out and retry, increasing downstream cost.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated) in us-east-1.
- Ingress fronted by internal edge proxy cluster behind api-gateway.
- Ephemeral-signed-url refresh service used by BrightEdge's orchestrator to rotate short-lived auth tokens every 60s.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Start 40 SSE clients that hold open streams for 30+ minutes.
2) Trigger scheduled batch upload coordinator that opens 150 parallel short HTTP/1.1 POSTs to /v1/embeddings for 10s windows.
3) Observe rate of 200->429 responses on aggregated requests from the tenant.

Expected behavior:
- Background credential refreshes and health probes should not cause tenant-level token-bucket depletion for burst windows.
- SSE long-lived connections should be prioritized (low-latency) and isolated from bulk ingestion traffic.

Actual behavior:
- Token-window accounting counts ephemeral auth refresh calls and health probe requests against the same per-tenant token bucket used for user traffic.
- A sawtooth pattern in the refill window coincides with the orchestrator refresh schedule (every 60s) causing cumulative exhaustion.

Relevant logs/observations provided by customer:
- Example 429 response headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; X-RateLimit-Reset: 21s; Retry-After: 21
- Edge logs:
  [2026-03-11T00:12:00Z] tenant=brightedge worker=auth-refresh path=/v1/auth/refresh status=200
  [2026-03-11T00:12:00Z] tenant=brightedge path=/v1/embeddings status=429 route=/embeddings-bulk
  [2026-03-11T00:12:01Z] tenant=brightedge path=/v1/stream/connect status=200 conn_id=xyz reconnect=1

Notes:
- Customer added that after reducing the refresh frequency to 300s the 429 rate drops but intermittent 429s still occur during concurrent scheduler windows.

Please see comments for interactive troubleshooting and SRE findings.
comments: 2026-03-11 09:15 UTC - Support(Asha): Opened ticket after initial triage with customer. Collected sample logs, request IDs, and timestamps. Asked customer for list of IPs and exact refresh schedule.

2026-03-11 11:02 UTC - SRE(Marco): Reproduced sawtooth refill pattern in tenant accounting on internal test harness by emulating 60s auth-refresh fanout plus bulk POSTs. Noted that healthcheck probes from the edge sidecar were not being excluded from rate accounting in dedicated pool config.
2026-03-11 14:28 UTC - Support(Asha): Customer confirms orchestration uses a burst of short-lived tokens; provided additional headers and example request-ids for 2026-03-10 23:05-23:15 UTC window.

2026-03-12 03:45 UTC - SRE(Marco): Applied a non-production config on canary nodes to ignore /v1/auth/refresh and internal healthcheck endpoints from tenant token-bucket counts. Early canary shows 90% reduction in 429s for synthetic run. Preparing patch.

2026-03-13 16:10 UTC - Support(Asha): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (rate-splitting guidance) and requested timeline for permanent fix. Asked for a formal runbook update to avoid regression post-upgrade.

2026-03-14 08:05 UTC - SRE(Marco): Deployed config change to customer dedicated pool (rolling restart with safe drain). Observed improvement in production: 429s dropped from 12% -> 0.8% during next scheduled run. Monitoring watch active for 48 hours.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses tested:
- H1: Healthcheck and orchestration refresh worker requests are counted against tenant's burst window -> confirmed in dedicated config.
- H2: Edge proxy connection reuse / HTTP/2 multiplexing incorrectly attributes background probe requests to primary API key -> some evidence in logs; correlated with shared connection pools.
- H3: Priority weighting between SSE route and embeddings-bulk route was not enforced for this tenant -> confirmed: route-weighting not applied when requests originate from internal signed-url host header.

Actions performed:
- Reproduced sawtooth refill in internal harness matching customer cadence.
- Tested excluding /v1/auth/refresh from token accounting on canary nodes.
- Adjusted route matching to respect host header for signed-url clients and applied route-weighting enforcement.
- Added a temporary token-window throttle exemption for internal-health endpoints on the dedicated pool.

Data points:
- Canary synthetic run with exemption: 429s reduced 92% compared to baseline.
- Production after rollout: 429s reduced to 0.8% during scheduled windows; SSE reconnects fell below 0.3% of total connections.
resolution:
Mitigation and fix applied:
1) Exempted internal auth-refresh and healthcheck endpoints from tenant token-bucket accounting in dedicated pool config.
2) Enforced route-weighting and host-based route isolation for signed-url clients so background workers are counted against a separate low-priority bucket.
3) Rolled configuration as a safe rolling restart with drain on dedicated nodes for BrightEdge.

Customer-facing workaround communicated: stagger auth-refresh frequency (>=120s) and switch to separate service account when possible to isolate background workers.

Status: Patch rolled to production 2026-03-14 07:50 UTC; monitoring window initiated for 48h. Post-deployment follow-up scheduled.
additional_actions:
Follow-ups and runbook updates:
- Update dedicated pool runbook: doc section 'Exclude internal health and auth-refresh endpoints from token accounting' (owner: infra-rate-team).
- Add a dashboard tile for per-tenant window refill and healthcheck accounting (owner: observability).
- Consider defaulting route isolation for signed-url origins in next major release.
- Postmortem scheduled if issue reoccurs after monitoring window ends.
